extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / natural philosophers (17th-century scientific readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and reporting natural-philosophy / scientific observations and short reports for a learned journal (e.g., anatomical observations, case reports, mathematical treatises). Emphasises empirical description, preparation methods, comparative evidence, and logical argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe preparation methods for anatomical observation
rubrics_metrics.description: This coat looks at first view indeed like a mucous substance; but if it be put into a crystal glass filled with clear water, and exposed to the light or sun, after the other coats are removed, this coat will be very well expanded (especially if the water be a little warm,) and will show all the fibrillse very fairly and distinctly, like the fine threads of lawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting microscopic/anatomical structure, state how specimens were prepared and examined (remove outer coats, place in clear water, warm slightly, expose to light) so readers can reproduce the observation and appreciate the fine fibrils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record detailed case history and symptoms for pathological reports
rubrics_metrics.description: I inquired about the situation of the stone, the age and condition of the horse, and whether the animal's urine was bloody, or whether he was troubled with strangury or suppression of urine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include situational details (location of lesion), subject age and condition, specific symptoms (e.g., bloody urine, strangury, suppression), husbandry/diet, and owner observations to support causal inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative anatomy and cross-species evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: For that the nerves decussate or cross one another, or that they are so blended together in their union, as to cause a confusion in their fibres, is not to be imagined; but those that are in the thalami optici on the right side run distinctly to the right eye, and those on the left accordingly. In many fishes the case is clear, where the 2 nerves are joined only by simple contact, and in the camelion not at all, as is said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support anatomical claims by comparing multiple species and noting differences (e.g., fishes, chameleon) to strengthen or weaken generalisations about structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain function by relating structure to mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: The superior fibre... are supposed to have the greatest flexure; ... the internal lateral fibres have less tension than the external, as before-mentioned. Hence it appears that the fibres that are parallel ... are as it were symphonical ... so that when any impression from an external object moves both fibres, it causes not a double sensation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link observed structural features (tension, flexure, relative size/position of fibres and muscles) to functional explanations (balance, single sensation) — provide mechanical/physical reasoning that connects form to function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear analogies to make physiological arguments intelligible
rubrics_metrics.description: I call fibrae Concordes... and answer to unisons in 2 viols or lutes, and therefore may be also called fibrae homotonae... so that when any impression from an external object moves both fibres, it causes not a double sensation, any more than unisons in 2 viols struck together cause a double sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ familiar analogies (musical unisons, instruments) to illustrate why observed correspondences produce single sensations or unified effects; explicitly map analogy elements to anatomical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit figure legends and label mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: an explanation of the Figure 4, pi. 15. — a a, bb, cc, dd, &c. are the fibrae Concordes of the optic nerves... ////, the two protuberances, called thalami nervorum opticorum... +, the place of their union; mm, the eyes divested of the sclerotica and uvea; nn, the processus ciliares...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including figures, give a full legend explaining each label and what it represents so readers can follow anatomical descriptions and cross-reference text and plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: When proposing causes or hypotheses, discuss alternatives and counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: What concerns their principal or original cause, he says, that that old opinion which supposes them to be a collection of vapours and exhalations put into a flame by the uppermost part of the air, is scarcely worth any consideration: for if the comets by such an inflammation should have their light of themselves, there could be given no reason why the tail should always be seen in opposition to the sun; ... Descartes's opinion, he says, is strange enough...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State alternative theories, point out observational contradictions, and explain why alternatives are inadequate; use empirical facts (parallax, eclipse behaviour, tail orientation) to justify preferred hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify methods and define technical terms in mathematical exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The quadrature... may be understood to be fourfold, viz. either by calculation, or by linear construction : and each of them again may be either perfectly exact, or else almost, or pretty near. The quadrature by accurate calculation, I call the analytical. That which is done by accurate construction, I call the geometrical. That which is done by calculation pretty near, I call the approach. That which is by construction pretty near, I call the mechanical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting mathematical or theoretical work, explicitly define categories of method and terminology (analytical, geometrical, mechanical, approach) so readers know the intended meaning and scope of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate convergence/error control for infinite-series results
rubrics_metrics.description: So that by continuing the series, the errors may be made less than a fraction given, and consequently less than any assignable quantity. Whence it follows, that the whole series must give the true value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using infinite series or approximations, show how partial sums bound the error and explain how errors shrink with further terms; include statements about alternating over- and under-estimates and how they converge to the true value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and compare prior work and claims of other authors
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several things relating to this quadrature, which might be taken notice of... Many indeed have professed to have found the true quadrature, as Cardinal Cusanus, Oron. Fineus, Jos. Scaliger, Tho. Gepherander, Tho. Hobbs, but all of them falsely, being disproved by the calculations of Archimedes, or by those of Ludolphus van Ceulen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention predecessors, credit earlier results, and state whether current findings confirm, extend, or refute earlier claims; provide comparisons or references to established calculations or observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include environmental and management factors when inferring causation in disease
rubrics_metrics.description: I imagine the person who took out the stone to be [anatomically] ignorant of the parts or their situation. ... he was constantly kept upon hay and other dry food, not having for some years been turned out to grass, which doubtless would have been of great service. Every year during spring and autumn he was observed to lose flesh...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In pathological case reports, record diet, workload, housing, and any repetitive exposures (e.g., hot dyed cloth on loins) as possible contributing causes; use such contextual data in causal reasoning.
